Cons: - Processor - playing Hungry Shark for 20 minutes caused the back of the phone to be very hot - JBL earphones - very cheaply made. Not worth the $50 "suggested retail price" per ZTE's website. My $10 skullcandy produced better sounds too - Button placement - I don't like the power button where it is. Hard to press. I'm always pressing the volume button along with the power button - Storage capacity - 32GB but really about 24GB free to use for personal stuff - Body - the backing is not completely flush. Seems to be in three pieces and on mine the top left piece is not perfectly flush to the middle piece. Kind of shows the lack of 100% QC. Final thoughts: Specs on paper are amazing, truly a flagship competitor. However, value doesn't hit a perfect score.
YMMV and who knows, you might like it more than I did. It certainly is a good value for the price but you'll get a lot more spending just a little more.

I loved this phone. That being said, if I hadn't used the Note 4 when trying to make the choice which phone to go with, I'd easily choose the G3. Setting up the phone itself was a breeze. It was a simple and easy basic Android setup experience that should be familiar to most people. The only interesting difference about the setup that I noticed is that it will try to have you set up face unlock as your primary security option and there is no option to set up your fingerprint unless you manually set it up in your settings AFTER the main setup is completed. Not a big issue, but it might be annoying if someone is expecting to set up their fingerprint during this beginning set up process. If you do decide to manually set up your fingerprint later, it is a longer and more tedious process than with other fingerprint readers, but it is equally as fast and accurate as most higher end fingerprint readers on the market once you get it ready.

To me, that's the biggest upgrade. Also worth noting is this phone still allows you to expand its memory with Micro SD cards. For me, that's a big consideration. I got the 64 GB version of the phone, which is plenty for now, but I know how quickly phones tend to fill up, and having the ability to add another two times that much storage (or more) at any time I want is great. This phone also still has an AUX 3.5 mm jack, so I can plug in on anyone's audio or car stereo setup without special adapters. The charger is still the ubiquitous Micro USB-B format, not the new USB-C hotness. Sometimes it's great to be an early adopter, but when it comes to chargers and audio input/output, it seems like being early is kind of a pain in the butt.
